title: How to do Authentication of Users in ASP.NET Core Identity
description: Implement login, logout, and return URL handling with ASP.NET Core Identity.

data.text: Authentication is the process of verifying a user's identity — confirming they are who they claim to be. In ASP.NET Core Identity this is done by validating a username/email and password against the AspNetUsers table, then issuing a signed authentication cookie.

terms.definition: High-level API for user authentication. Handles password verification, cookie creation, and external login sign-in.
Validates the user's password and signs them in if correct. Returns a SignInResult indicating success or failure.
The URL the user originally requested before being redirected to the login page. Identity appends it as a query string.
When enabled, the authentication cookie's expiry is renewed on each request, keeping active users signed in.

data.text: We inject UserManager<AppUser> and SignInManager<AppUser> into the controller. The Login GET action renders the form; the POST action validates credentials and issues the cookie. The Logout action calls SignOutAsync to remove the cookie.

data.title: Exercise: Build the Login / Logout Flow
data.description: Wire up a full login and logout experience using SignInManager.
steps: Create the Login.cs view model with Email, Password, ReturnUrl, and Remember properties.
Create AccountController with Login (GET + POST) and Logout (POST) actions.
Use FindByEmailAsync to locate the user, then PasswordSignInAsync to authenticate.
Add a RememberMe checkbox and pass it as the third argument of PasswordSignInAsync.
Create the Login.cshtml view and the Secured.cshtml view with a logout form.
Configure the Identity cookie timeout in Program.cs.
data.expectedOutcome: Users can log in with email and password, are redirected back to the originally requested page, and can log out to clear the authentication cookie.

items.question: What is the difference between SignInAsync and PasswordSignInAsync?
items.answer: SignInAsync is a low-level method that writes a cookie from a ClaimsPrincipal you provide. PasswordSignInAsync is a higher-level Identity method that finds the user, verifies the password hash, and then signs the user in — all in one call.

items.question: Why call SignOutAsync before PasswordSignInAsync?
items.answer: If the user is already signed in under a different account, calling SignOutAsync first clears the old cookie so the new sign-in starts from a clean state.

items.question: What does the false parameter in PasswordSignInAsync mean?
items.answer: It is the lockoutOnFailure flag. Passing false means failed login attempts will not lock the user account. Set it to true in production for brute-force protection.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: SignInManager<AppUser> is the primary API for logging users in and out.
PasswordSignInAsync handles password verification and cookie creation together.
ReturnUrl ensures users land back on the page they originally requested.
ConfigureApplicationCookie controls timeout, sliding expiration, and redirect paths.
data.takeaway: Users can now log in and out. Next, manage those users with roles and claims for fine-grained authorization.
